title: [native_aot][4/7] gen_aot_lib: the generated kernel source

Human note:

Real work! Generate launchers and conditional gating functions in C++ for embedding.

Claude note:

The first half of the generator: a declaration plus its sidecars become the C++
ATen links. Source production only -- the CLI and the emitted CMake are next, so
this reads as "what is generated and why".

gen_op emits one .cpp per declaration: a marshalling launcher per kernel (from the
sidecar kind's Toolchain, so the guard chain is toolchain-blind), an early-out over
the shipped capabilities, then one cond chain per capability ending in `return
false` so the op falls through to aten.

The same declaration also emits a covers() predicate, so the router can ask
whether the AOT path applies without entering it. Its signature comes from
torchgen's structured introspection rather than being written out per op, which is
what makes it the signature aten will really call -- including for an op whose meta
function precomputes arguments.

Two gates are generated rather than written per declaration. The device gate
compares exact major.minor, because sm_103 reports major 10: a major-only gate
offered it sm_100 artifacts and the module load then failed instead of declining,
with no retry. The size gate exists because a kind whose exported ABI narrows
shapes to int32 cannot be handed a dim past INT32_MAX; it is per-kind and
per-argument, the width being a property of that ABI rather than of aten.

Test Plan:

```
pytest tools/test/test_native_aot_tools.py
```

Run at this commit's own tree, in a checkout with no built torch -- which is
what lint.yml's "Test tools" job has. This commit's tests cover the emitted
launchers and per-capability cond chains, the device gate comparing exact
major.minor, the shipped-versus-declared arch selector, the covers() predicate's
signature and the device it reads, and the int32 size gate being per-kind and
per-argument.

Authored with an AI assistant (Claude Code).
